slot.brief: Phenol + CHCl3/NaOH followed by hydrolysis: identify the product and the reaction name (Reimer–Tiemann).

stem: Phenol on treatment with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification yields a compound $X$. Identify $X$ and the name of the reaction.

verdicts.working: CHCl3 + aq NaOH generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl2), which attacks phenoxide at the ortho position; hydrolysis of the -CHCl2 intermediate and acidification gives o-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde). This is the Reimer–Tiemann reaction. Kolbe's reaction (CO2/NaOH) would give salicylic acid instead.

working:
When phenol is treated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$), the electrophilic intermediate dichlorocarbene ($:\!\text{CCl}_2$) attacks the phenoxide ring preferentially at the *ortho*-position:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3\,/\,\text{NaOH}} o\text{-}\text{NaO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHCl}_2$$
Alkaline hydrolysis of the dichloromethyl intermediate converts it to the aldehyde group:
$$o\text{-}\text{NaO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHCl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} o\text{-}\text{NaO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO}$$
Subsequent acidification yields salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde):
$$o\text{-}\text{NaO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} o\text{-}\text{HO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO} \text{ (salicylaldehyde)}$$
This transformation is called the Reimer–Tiemann reaction.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A confuses the reagents ($\text{CHCl}_3/\text{NaOH}$) with Kolbe's reaction ($\text{CO}_2/\text{NaOH}$), which produces salicylic acid.
Option C correctly identifies the reaction name as Reimer–Tiemann, but names salicylic acid (which is obtained if $\text{CCl}_4$ is used instead of $\text{CHCl}_3$).
Option D correctly identifies the product as salicylaldehyde, but misnames the reaction as Kolbe's reaction.
